key_insight: A physics-based, multi-mode lookup framework replaces detailed chemical kinetics while representing combustion, shocks, and expansion in rotating detonation engines.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a path toward less expensive rotating detonation engine simulations while retaining sensitivity to local thermodynamic conditions.
method: Precompute thermochemical states and reaction source terms for lookup from conserved flow variables.
Use homogeneous reactor solutions for deflagration and post-detonation reactions up to the Chapman–Jouguet state.
Model supersonic relaxation beyond the Chapman–Jouguet state with equilibrium isentropic expansion.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with detailed chemistry span homogeneous ignition, one-dimensional detonations, and a two-dimensional engine, showing agreement in ignition delays, detonation propagation, and streamline thermodynamic evolution.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantified computational speedup, and accuracy outside the evaluated thermodynamic and mixture conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Physics-based Tabulation Approach for Rotating Detonation Engines
